title: NVIDIA Launches Cosmos 3, Open Foundation Model for Physical AI
summary: NVIDIA launched Cosmos 3 on May 31, 2026 at GTC Taipei, an open world foundation model for physical AI built on a mixture-of-transformers architecture that unifies vision reasoning, world generation, and action prediction in a single system. The company describes it as the first fully open omnimodel that natively understands and generates text, images, video, ambient sound, and actions, trained on billions of samples across those modalities. It ships as Cosmos 3 Super and Cosmos 3 Nano, with a 4-billion-parameter Cosmos 3 Edge variant for real-time on-device inference following on July 20, 2026. Alongside the launch, NVIDIA formed the Cosmos Coalition with Agile Robots, Black Forest Labs, Generalist, LTX, Runway, and Skild AI to jointly develop future open world models. NVIDIA said Cosmos 3 leads open-model leaderboards including Physics-IQ, PAI-Bench, RoboArena, and VANTAGE-Bench.
whyItMatters: Cosmos 3 folds three previously separate jobs -- understanding a scene, simulating how it evolves, and predicting the actions needed to act in it -- into a single open model, which NVIDIA says cuts physical AI training and evaluation cycles from months to days. Because the weights are freely downloadable and a coalition of labs, including watchlist names Generalist and Skild AI, is committed to building on it, Cosmos 3 is positioned to become shared infrastructure for robot learning and synthetic data generation across the industry, the way open large language models did for text.
